items.action: Build after upgrading, and rename or mark `override` every member of yours the compiler reports as colliding.
items.note: All three pickers gained members for the new inputs and outputs. Subclassing a DS component is unsupported but consumers do it, and a redeclared member collides whether it is public or protected. The compiler enumerates every collision, so a build is the whole check and no list here could stay current.
items.appliesWhen: You subclass a picker component. Template users of the `<ds-...>` elements need nothing.
items.pitfall: `protected` is no protection: a redeclared protected member collides exactly as a public one does.
items.verify: The app builds with no TS2415 or TS2416 naming a picker component.

items.action: Nothing unless you subclass ToastRegionComponent and declare a member of those names: rename yours, or add `override` if you meant to replace ours.
items.note: ToastRegionComponent gained `timers`, `position` and `newestFirst`: the auto-dismiss countdown moved into the region, because only it knows when a toast became visible — started in the service, a toast queued behind `maxVisible` expired without ever being shown. `newestFirst` puts the newest toast nearest the anchor.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class that extends ToastRegionComponent.
items.pitfall: `durationMs` is now a required field on `ToastEntry`. That reaches further than subclassing, so it is its own item — see `toast-entry-duration-required`.
items.verify: Build your app: no TS4114 or TS2415 against a class extending ToastRegionComponent.

items.action: Add `durationMs` to every hand-built `ToastEntry`: the auto-dismiss delay in ms, or `0` for indefinite. `ToastService.show()` and its variants are unaffected — they take `ToastOptions`, where `durationMs` stays optional and defaults to 5000 (0 for `loading`).
items.note: The field moved from optional to required because the countdown moved out of the service and into the region: only the region knows when a toast became VISIBLE, and started in the service a toast queued behind `maxVisible` expired while still waiting. An entry now has to carry its own delay. `ToastEntry` is exported and `ToastRegionComponent.add()` is public, so this is reachable without subclassing anything.
items.appliesWhen: You reference the `ToastEntry` type — annotating a variable, building one to pass to `add()`, or mapping your own model onto it. Callers of `ToastService` need nothing.
items.pitfall: The break is a compile error at the construction site, not at `add()`, so a search for `add(` finds nothing. And `0` is not the same as leaving it out: it means indefinite, so a toast written that way never dismisses itself.
items.verify: The app builds with no TS2741 or TS2739 naming `durationMs` on `ToastEntry`.

informational: All three pickers scroll the keyboard cursor into view by default; scrollActiveIntoView="false" turns it off.
Home and End now work on ds-multi-select and ds-autocomplete, which only ds-select had.
ds-autocomplete takes compareWith for object values; the default stays === so string and number values are unaffected.
New on all three pickers: loading, opened, closed. New on the two that filter: filterWith (a predicate, or "none" for a server-filtered list) and filterChange.
ds-multi-select and ds-autocomplete gained name, readOnly (with its readonly binding alias) and clearable, which were ds-select-only.
New slots on all three pickers: dsPanelHeaderTemplate, dsPanelFooterTemplate, dsGroupLabelTemplate.
The option row is tokenised: --ds-option-gap, --ds-option-padding, --ds-option-radius, --ds-option-row-gap, --ds-option-bg-color-active.
ds-multi-select no longer carries its own panel rules at all; --ds-multi-select-option-bg-color-active is an alias of the shared --ds-option-bg-color-active and still works.
The select-all row now reads the option row's gap and padding, so it lines up with the options below it; it was one step wider before.
DsOption gained disabledReason, announced through aria-describedby on a disabled row.
Type-ahead is on ds-select and ds-multi-select, not ds-autocomplete, whose trigger is a text field.
PageUp and PageDown move the cursor ten rows on all three pickers; none had them.
clear() is public on all three pickers now; it empties the value and does not move focus.
scrollActiveIntoView follows the KEYBOARD only — the rows also set the active index on mouseenter, and reacting to that pulled a half-visible row under the pointer.
aria-multiselectable stays absent from ds-select on purpose: ARIA permits it only on a multi-value listbox. docs/picker-contract.md states this so nobody adds it to satisfy the audit.
ds-table takes expandMode="single" to keep one row open at a time; the default stays "multiple", which is what it did before.
ds-table takes expandAllToggle to put an expand-all chevron in the expander column header; it is page-scoped when paginating, like select-all, and is suppressed under expandMode="single".
ds-table emits (rowExpanded) and (rowCollapsed), expand-all included. Neither fires for a collapse the host writes into expandedIds itself, nor for an id whose row is not in data().
ds-table announces "N rows expanded" in its live region from two rows up; a single expander already says so through its own aria-expanded.

ds-table no longer puts `skeleton-mode` on its host element. Nothing in the library styled it: the rule it switched on suppressed a row hover that used to reach every row, and that hover now needs `.clickable`, which a skeleton row never has. Only a consumer reaching in through ::ng-deep would notice.

The column-resize handle now carries aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax alongside aria-valuenow, all in px, while it has focus. A focusable role="separator" is a range widget, so a bare pixel value was being announced against ARIA's implicit 0-100.

ds-loading-overlay now marks the content it covers `inert` while loading, so the keyboard cannot reach what the scrim already hides from the pointer. Anything focusable behind the scrim stops being tabbable and leaves the accessibility tree until loading ends; `aria-busy` on the host is unaffected.

inertContent="false" on ds-loading-overlay turns that off, for a scrim that covers only part of its content — the consumer then owns marking the covered subtree. ds-table does this: its scrim starts below the header, and only `<tbody>` goes inert, so sorting and filtering during a refresh still work.

ds-table's column resize now stops at the width of the scroll viewport, on both the pointer and the keyboard path. It was unbounded before. The bound exists so the handle's aria-valuemax is true — a focusable role="separator" is a range widget, and it had been announcing a ceiling nothing applied.
